columns: This spreadsheet compares the velocity measurements of the SPICE duct conducted by NASA in 2008(The data folder is SPICE_AIRFLOW_TEST) and Yale in 2009. The measured points of the two measurements are not exactly spatially coincident. Therefore linear interpolation is used for normal gravity data to spatially match the probe points.
This spreadsheet compares the velocity m: It is shown that from the comparison, the Yale velocity is pretty close to the NASA velocity at different probe points except right above the nozzle. It seems like the measurements by NASA are with nozzle in the setup, however the nozzle was removed in the Yale measurements.
It is also shown that the Fan setting is a better parameter to rely on while comparing the flow velcocity measurements between Yale data and NASA data.
The velocity has been re-measured in Oct 2012 with a 1.6 mm nozzle in the setup.
